culture.name: Ecuador
culture.language: Spanish, Kichwa or your home language
culture.timeDifference: It is about the same time there, give or take an hour.
culture.homeTravelNote: a flight of several hours, close enough that home feels within reach

cookLines: Potatoes soften in the pot with onion and achiote, and the whole apartment smells like home.
You taste the locro and stir in a little more cheese, the way your grandmother would.
{roommate} wanders in and asks what smells so good.
You share bowls at the counter with slices of avocado on top, and for an hour the world is small and warm.

festivals.title: Día de los Difuntos
festivals.body: On 2 November, families at home visit the cemetery and share colada morada and guaguas de pan in memory of the people they miss. Here it is midterm season.
festivals.join: Share colada morada with the Ecuadorian community in town.
festivals.joinText: Someone's aunt has made a pot big enough for fifty. You hold the warm purple cup in both hands and talk about your grandfather.
festivals.host: Make colada morada and guaguas de pan with friends.
festivals.hostText: Blackberries, blueberries and spices simmer for hours. Your friends decorate the little bread figures with far too much icing.
festivals.skip: Light a candle and call home.
festivals.skipText: Your mother tells you who came to the cemetery this year. You raise a mug of tea to the screen.

festivals.title: Año Viejo
festivals.body: At home 31 December means a paper and sawdust figure of the old year on every corner, ready to burn at midnight, and twelve grapes for twelve wishes. Campus is quiet and cold.
festivals.join: Spend New Year's Eve with an Ecuadorian family.
festivals.joinText: There is no bonfire, but the children have made a small paper año viejo and everyone cheers when it is torn up at midnight. You eat your twelve grapes too fast.
festivals.host: Host a New Year's Eve dinner for students who could not travel.
festivals.hostText: You hand out grapes and explain the wishes. At midnight someone runs around the block with an empty suitcase, hoping for a year of travel.
festivals.skip: Call home at midnight and go to bed.
festivals.skipText: Through the phone you hear the firecrackers and the whole street counting down. You make your wishes quietly.

festivals.title: Carnaval
festivals.body: At home Carnaval means two days off, water and foam in the streets, music and plates of fritada. It falls in the middle of the term this year.
festivals.join: Go to the student association's Carnaval party.
festivals.joinText: Someone has brought cans of foam, and nobody stays clean for long. You laugh until your sides ache.
festivals.host: Cook for friends and put on the music from home.
festivals.hostText: Your friends try mote and fried plantain and ask what Carnaval is like in your town. You talk for an hour.
festivals.skip: Look through the family photos and keep studying.
festivals.skipText: Your cousins are soaked and covered in foam in every picture. You save them all.

familyCall: Quito is on almost the same clock as the East Coast, so your mother calls right after lunch.
She asks if you are eating well and reminds you to dress warmly.
Your little cousin grabs the phone to show you a drawing, and your grandmother asks when you are coming home.
You hang up homesick and a little lighter.
culture.homeMoneyNote: Ecuador uses the US dollar, so money from home arrives without an exchange rate to worry about, only transfer fees.
culture.familySupportNote: Designed value, kept at the India baseline of 1.0. The research has no sourced figure that would justify more or less family support for Ecuadorian students. Flight costs are handled by roundTripFlightUsd, not by this factor.

entryNotes.F1: About 3,282 Ecuadorians studied in the US in 2024/25, the 42nd largest group, and Ecuadorian nationals received 2,014 F-1 visas in FY2024.
entryNotes.H1B: Ecuadorian nationals received 299 H-1B visas in FY2024, and Ecuadorians wait in the shorter Rest of World green card queue, not India's or China's.
entryNotes.B2: Ecuador is not in the Visa Waiver Program, so Ecuadorians cannot use ESTA and need a visitor visa before any trip.
entryNotes.O1: Ecuadorian nationals received 60 O-1 visas in FY2024, up from 24 in FY2018.
entryNotes.FAM: Ecuador is charged to the Rest of World queue and, unlike Brazil, Colombia and Venezuela, was eligible for the DV-2026 Diversity Visa lottery.
entryNotes.EWI: Border Patrol encounters of Ecuadorians at the southwest border fell from 116,144 in FY2024 to 2,446 in FY2026, and entering without inspection usually blocks a green card from inside the US later.
entryNotes.ASY: In FY2024 immigration courts granted 657 and denied 2,774 asylum cases from Ecuadorian nationals, about 19 percent of decisions.

facts.title: Time difference to Quito
facts.text: Quito is on UTC-5 all year with no daylight saving time. It is level with US Eastern in winter and 1 hour behind in summer, and 3 hours ahead of Pacific in winter and 2 in summer.

facts.title: Round-trip flight, Ecuador to US
facts.text: Design estimate of $650. No sourced fare range for Ecuador to US round trips was found in the research; real fares vary widely by route and season.

facts.title: F-1 visas issued to Ecuadorians
facts.text: Ecuadorian nationals received 2,014 F-1 visas in FY2024, the highest of recent years, and 1,633 in FY2025. Figures are State Department data republished by VisaGrader.

facts.title: Ecuadorian students in the US
facts.text: Open Doors counted 3,282 Ecuadorian students in US higher education in 2024/25, up from 3,256 the year before, the 42nd largest group.

facts.title: Remittances to Ecuador
facts.text: Ecuador received $7.729 billion in remittances in 2025, a record and 18.2 percent more than in 2024. About 77.8 percent, or $6.01 billion, came from the United States (Banco Central del Ecuador, as reported).

facts.title: H-1B visas for Ecuadorians
facts.text: Ecuadorian nationals received 299 H-1B visas in FY2024 and 302 in FY2025, up from 130 in FY2018. Ecuador's share of all H-1B approvals was not found; many people switch status inside the US without a visa stamp.

facts.title: Asylum decisions for Ecuadorian applicants
facts.text: In FY2024 immigration courts granted 657 and denied 2,774 asylum cases from Ecuadorian nationals, about 19 percent of decisions. Another 3,683 were not adjudicated. Individual claims matter more than averages.

facts.title: Family green card queue for Ecuador
facts.text: Ecuador is charged to the Rest of World queue, with no separate column in the Visa Bulletin. November 2026 final action dates as transcribed by a law firm: adult children of citizens (F1) 22 Jan 2021, married children (F3) 22 Oct 2015, siblings (F4) 22 Oct 2012. A sibling petition filed today faces a wait of roughly 14 years.

facts.title: Border Patrol encounters of Ecuadorian nationals
facts.text: Border Patrol recorded 113,813 encounters of Ecuadorian nationals at the southwest border in FY2023, 116,144 in FY2024, 7,757 in FY2025 and 2,446 in FY2026. Totals are summed from CBP's public encounters file.

mechanics.asylumNote: 657 grants and 2,774 denials in immigration court, FY2024 (657 of 3,431 decisions, 19.1 percent); 3,683 more not adjudicated. EOIR Asylum Decisions by Nationality, https://www.justice.gov/eoir/media/1344846/dl
